Plan legend & over-sideboarding rules
Turbo
Execute the combo / lethal plan at maximum speed. Interaction is there to force a window, not to grind.
Slow
Removal and resource exchanges matter. Preserve engine density and expect the game to last longer.
Control
Find a lock piece or interaction first, then execute our normal plan. Teeg/Ouphe plans often fall here.
Over-sideboarding
0–4 changes: normal
5: review density
6+: deliberate transformation only

Core heuristics

Doomsday / Oracle

Keep Ouphe for LED/Petal. Cut Vibrance and the grind package. Snuff Out can force Thassa's Oracle piles to account for reduced blue devotion if Oracle dies before its trigger resolves.

Massacre / white-source rule

Do not expose a Plains type unnecessarily against UB decks with Massacre. The current build removes Savannah entirely. Teeg becomes primarily a GSZ bullet; a naturally drawn Teeg can be discarded to Speaker.

Hogaak package

If Hogaak comes in, keep all 3 Formidable Speakers by default. Speaker is part of the Hogaak package because it converts a low-value card into the tutorable 8/8 grind threat.

Vibrance / mana-lock rule

Default: Vibrance is a flex cut when the matchup does not attack our mana. Keep it against Wasteland. Also keep it when it has a specific land-lock job: versus Back to Basics it tutors Boseiju; versus Magus of the Moon, Magus itself can enable RR so Vibrance becomes a tutorable 3-damage answer.

Mass-critical principle

Against fair decks, 2–4 cards is the default. Five changes demand a reason. Six or more means we are deliberately transforming the deck.

Hogaak vs UB

Speaker can tutor Hogaak after the first wave of interaction. Current UB removal is poor at exiling or cleanly answering an 8/8 black/green threat. Do not bring Hogaak into Swords/Karakas shells.

Snuff Out

Tempo removal, not generic fair-deck removal. Best when zero mana lets us continue Cub/GSZ/NO development. Remember: nonblack target only.

Natural Order

Four by default. Go to three against hard tempo when duplicate NO is too costly. Do not cut it by reflex against mana-denial decks.

Visionary + Sabertooth loop

Keep in long games and against Tron/Lands. Cut when Bowmasters/hard tempo make a 4-mana loop package unrealistic.

Gaddock Teeg

Teeg is a Control-plan bullet, not a passive value creature. It shuts off our own GSZ/NO after resolving. Find it first, lock the opponent, then use Sabertooth if we need to unlock our own spells.

Sweepers

Always check the orange warning before committing the fourth/fifth creature. Massacre, Wrath of the Skies, Eldrazi Confluence, Fury, Brotherhood's End, Terminus, Supreme Verdict and Toxic Deluge-style effects all change sequencing.

Caller of the Claw

Caller is not in the current 75, but its relevance is tracked matchup-by-matchup. If sweeper density remains high in real testing, Caller becomes a serious candidate because Speaker/OUAT can access it.

Thoughtseize compression

The main reason to stay BG: the same four slots cover Reanimator, Show, Aluren, Doomsday, TES and Tron. Do not side it in just because the opponent is blue or black.

Leyline + Endurance split

Leyline gives turn-zero power while Endurance remains a creature/engine card and a usable topdeck. Thoughtseize covers Show-and-Tell transformation plans that bypass graveyard hate.

Read each route from top to bottom. Mana badges show the pool after each step. A–D are distinct discardable cards.

Hand requirements and sequencing notes
  • Start with seven cards, without a mulligan. T1 cards must be available on T1; other cards must arrive before use. Tutor targets must remain in the library.
  • The play route requires Quirion in hand. Tutoring for it consumes another search and discard. Without it, the three-Symbiote route requires a fourth discard unavailable from the eight cards seen.
  • Quirion returns Forest/Bayou, not a sacrificed fetchland. The recovered permanent supplies a discard; it is not an extra draw. Boseiju is not a Forest and cannot be returned this way.
  • Stay in the same T2 main phase. Earthbend does not untap Cradle. Speaker is in hand when Cradle taps after each bounce; do not count it. Cub’s extra green is included in all totals.
  • Symbiote can untap the animated Cradle. Speaker has summoning sickness: never use its tap ability in these T2 lines.

Alternative Speaker exits

Shared end state: Five creatures: dork, Cub, animated Cradle, Speaker and Symbiote. First land, dork and Cradle are tapped. Symbiote has used its activation for this turn. Speaker cannot use its tap ability on T2, including after being replayed.

A — Find Hoof: prepare T3

Use the second Speaker search for Craterhoof Behemoth and keep it in hand. End T2 with five creatures and Hoof ready for T3.

The remaining 2 mana is available only now; it does not carry into T3. On T3, even first land (1) + dork/Arbor (2 with Cub) + Cradle (6) gives 9 mana before using any untap abilities, enough to hardcast Hoof if the board survives.

Two discards total. Hoof is tutored; it need not be drawn.

B — Find another Cub: grow the board

Use the second search for Badgermole Cub. Spend the remaining 2 mana to cast it and earthbend the first land.

End T2 with seven creatures: dork, two Cubs, Speaker, Symbiote and both lands. The first land remains tapped: earthbend grants haste but does not untap it. No mana remains in this line.

Two discards total. Maximum board development among these three exits; Hoof has not been tutored.

C — Find Quirion: hardcast Hoof on T2

Requires Hoof already in hand and a Forest to return. With the first land being a Forest, search for Quirion Ranger, cast it for G and keep G floating.

Return the tapped Forest with Quirion to untap animated Cradle. Six creatures remain: dork, Cub, Cradle, Speaker, Symbiote and Quirion. Tap Cradle for 6 + Cub's 1 = 7; together with the floating G, you have 8 mana to hardcast Hoof.

2 − 1 + 7 = 8 → Craterhoof in T2.

Combat: This is not automatically lethal. With this exact sequence only Hoof can attack: the dork and Cradle are tapped, and the other creatures entered this turn. Hoof sees seven creatures and attacks as a 12/12 trampler.

Two discards plus Hoof already in hand. Do not discard Hoof to either Speaker trigger.

Hand budget

The five setup cards are the first land, dork/GSZ, Cradle, Cub and Speaker. Add two distinct discardable cards: seven cards cover exits A and B. The searches replace each discarded card with the creature you need; returning and recasting Speaker does not supply discard fodder.

Exit C additionally needs Hoof: eight cards total by T2. On the play, an opening seven plus the normal T2 draw can supply exactly that set; there is no spare card beyond the two discards. For example, open the five setup cards + Hoof + one discardable card, and discard the T2 draw as the second card. Required cards must arrive before their respective play/search.

Speaker's tap ability is never used here. Symbiote can untap Cradle because it is a creature after earthbend. The five-mana activation happens while Speaker is in hand; count four creatures, not five.

Sabertooth Loop

Speaker loop · net +2 green per cycle

Entry state: eight creatures, Speaker on the battlefield, Cradle tapped, Symbiotes used, and three green floating. This is the endpoint of either T2 route above.

  1. A · Reset one Symbiote

    Pay to Sabertooth to return a Symbiote. Recast it for . As a new object, it can activate again.

    0 × floatingFirst cycle: spend the initial 3 green

  2. B · Bounce Speaker → untap Cradle

    Activate the new Symbiote: return Speaker and untap Cradle. Seven creatures remain. Tap Cradle: 7 + Cub’s 1 = 8 green.

    8 × floatingSpeaker in hand

  3. C · Recast Speaker → repeat

    Cast Speaker . Resolve its ETB without discarding or searching. Eight creatures are back on the battlefield.

    5 × floatingSame entry state · 2 more green
8 produced − 3 Speaker − 2 bounce − 1 Symbiote = +2 per cycle ↻

Repeat a finite number of times large enough for the finish. No further discard fodder is needed.

Finish · use the pending ETB only here

  1. 1 · Cast Speaker; keep its ETB on the stack

    After accumulating enough mana, respond to the ETB by paying to Sabertooth. Return Speaker to your hand.

  2. 2 · Discard that Speaker → find Hoof

    Resolve the pending ETB. Discard Speaker itself and find Craterhoof Behemoth. No additional card is required.

  3. 3 · Cast Hoof → repeat ETBs → attack

    Cast Hoof for . With enough mana, return it for and recast it repeatedly. Its boosts accumulate; Hoof has haste and gains trample. This produces lethal T2 combat damage on an unobstructed goldfish board.

Visionary variant · draw through the deck

Badgermole Cub + Temur Sabertooth + Wirewood Symbiote + Elvish Visionary + earthbent untapped Gaea's Cradle

Five creatures are in play including Cradle. Tap Cradle for 5, Cub adds 1 → 6 mana. Symbiote returns Visionary and untaps Cradle. Sabertooth returns Symbiote for 2, recast Symbiote for 1, recast Visionary for 2 and draw.

Loop cost = 5 · output = 6 → +1 green mana +1 card per cycle
Endurance turns the completed engine into a recursive endgame: recycle Boseiju / graveyard resources and avoid decking.

MyMTGO is used as the main source for current opposing 75s and post-board warnings. Where the exact archetype in the friend's blueprint does not map cleanly to a current MyMTGO page, the guide labels the row as family-level, inference, or TBC instead of pretending the information is exact.

RC3 archetype clarifications: GB Mole = the wider GB Mole / Cradle Control family; Key Ring = Colorless Tron; 8 Moon = Mono-Red Stompy / red prison.

Macro taxonomy (RC3 proposal): the grouping is strategic rather than purely taxonomic. Current MyMTGO has Energy, Mono-U Tron, Dimir Midrange/Tempo, Doomsday, Lands, D&T, Show and Tell, Aluren, Eldrazi, Beanstalk and Izzet all represented near the top of the format, so the guide groups them by the sideboarding problem they create rather than by color alone.

Sweeper watchlist: Wrath of the Skies is currently recorded across White Beanstalk, D&T, Stiflenought, Bant/UW shells and some Energy configurations. Eldrazi Confluence is present in current Initiative/Eldrazi lists. Current Show-family sideboards include Brotherhood's End and Fury. Massacre appears in current UB sideboards. Terminus, Supreme Verdict and Toxic Deluge remain low-frequency but relevant control/midrange sweepers and should always trigger a play-around check when the opponent's colors/archetype support them.
